agency:       The rawest material is the café's own facts: the real shift schedule, the busiest hours from the till or POS reports, the menu and equipment (espresso machine model, grinder), the actual hourly rate and tip split, and the owner's description of what a great barista does on a Saturday rush. None of this is in this workspace, so I will use clearly marked placeholders (shop name, location, pay, hours) and assume a small independent café with a mix of weekday-morning and weekend shifts.

acceleration: Use the standard structure of a high-converting local-hire post: a plain-language title with the location and "part-time," then "What you'll do," "What we're looking for," "What you get," and "How to apply." The closest proxies: check every placeholder against the real schedule and pay before posting, confirm the pay range and any required disclosures meet local law, and have the owner or a current barista read it and say "yes, this is the job." After posting, the number of qualified applicants in the first week is the real test.

answers.plain:
# Part-Time Barista

**Location:** [Cafe Name], [Address/Neighborhood]
**Hours:** Part-time, 15–25 hours/week, including some early mornings and weekends
**Pay:** $[X]–$[Y]/hour plus tips
**Start date:** [Date]

## About Us

[Cafe Name] is a neighborhood coffee shop serving carefully sourced espresso, seasonal drinks, and fresh-baked pastries. We're a small, friendly team that cares about good coffee and even better conversations with the people who come through our door.

## What You'll Do

- Prepare espresso drinks, brewed coffee, tea, and other beverages to our recipes and quality standards
- Greet customers warmly, take orders, and handle payments at the register
- Keep the bar, seating area, and restrooms clean and well stocked
- Open or close the shop, including cash handling and end-of-shift cleaning
- Help with inventory, restocking, and receiving deliveries
- Follow food safety and sanitation guidelines

## What We're Looking For

- A positive, patient attitude, especially during the morning rush
- Ability to work quickly and accurately in a fast-paced setting
- Reliability and punctuality
- Comfort working as part of a small team
- Ability to stand for long periods and lift up to 25 lbs
- Availability for at least [two] weekend shifts per month

**Nice to have:** previous barista or food service experience, latte art skills, or a food handler's card. We're happy to train the right person, so enthusiasm matters more than experience.

## What We Offer

- Competitive hourly pay plus tips
- Free drinks during shifts and a discount on food and beans
- Paid training from experienced baristas
- Flexible scheduling with advance notice
- A supportive, fun team and room to grow, including into shift lead roles

## How to Apply

Send a short introduction and your availability to [email address], or stop by [Cafe Name] and ask for [Name]. A resume is welcome but not required.

*[Cafe Name] is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and are happy to provide accommodations during the hiring process.*

---

I left placeholders for the details only you know (name, pay, hours, contact). If you tell me the cafe's name, location, and vibe, I can tailor the tone, or I can write a shorter version for Indeed or Instagram.
answers.nudge:
# Part-Time Barista at [Café Name]

**[Neighborhood, City] · Part-time · 12-25 hrs/week · $[X]-$[Y]/hr + tips (tips averaged ~$[Z]/hr last quarter)**

## The short version

We're a [number]-seat neighborhood café that pulls about [N] shots a day, roasts nothing, and cares a lot about getting the small things right: a properly dialed-in espresso, a name remembered, a clean bar at close. We're looking for a part-time barista to join a team of [N] people. You'll be trained properly, paid fairly, and given real room to grow if you want it.

No experience? Apply anyway. We hire for attitude and teach the rest.

## What a shift looks like

- **Make drinks well and consistently.** Espresso, milk steaming, pour-over, batch brew, and seasonal specials. You'll learn to taste a shot and adjust the grinder, not just follow a recipe card.
- **Run the front of the café.** Greet people, take orders, handle the register, and make regulars feel known and newcomers feel welcome.
- **Keep the space ready.** Opening and closing routines, restocking, cleaning, and food safety. Unglamorous, and it's what makes the café feel good.
- **Work as a team.** Call out orders, back up whoever is slammed, and flag problems early.

## Schedule

- Typically 3-4 shifts a week, 4-6 hours each
- We need coverage on **weekend mornings** (6:30 am-2 pm) and **some weekday afternoons** (11 am-5 pm)
- Schedules are posted **2 weeks ahead** and never changed with less than 48 hours' notice, apart from emergencies
- Shift swaps go through [app/group chat], with no manager approval needed if the swap is covered
- Students welcome. Tell us your class schedule and we'll build around it.

## You might be a great fit if you

- Stay calm and friendly when the line is out the door
- Care how things taste and look, even at 7 am
- Take feedback well and like getting better at a craft
- Show up on time and communicate when plans change
- Can stand for a full shift and lift 25 lbs (we'll make reasonable accommodations)
- Are [age] or older and can work legally in [country/state]

**Nice to have, not required:** prior café or food-service experience, latte art, a food handler card (we'll pay for it if you don't have one), or a second language spoken in our neighborhood.

## What you get

- **Pay:** $[X]-$[Y]/hr depending on experience, plus 100% of tips, pooled weekly
- **Paid training:** about 3 shifts alongside a trainer, with a written skills checklist so you always know where you stand
- **Raises:** a review at 90 days, then every 6 months. The path to Lead Barista is spelled out, and it comes with a pay bump.
- **Free drinks on shift** and a [discount/free bag of beans] each week
- **A meal break** on any shift over 5 hours
- **Learning on our dime:** cuppings, a milk and latte art workshop, and paid time to attend [local coffee event] if you're interested
- **Paid sick leave** as required by [state/city law] [or: beyond the legal minimum]
- **A team that likes each other,** with staff outings, a say in the seasonal menu, and a manager who works the bar too

## How to apply

1. Send a short note to **[email]** or apply at **[link]**. Tell us about a time you made someone's day better, at work or anywhere else. Three or four sentences is plenty. A résumé is welcome but optional.
2. Include your **availability** (days and hours you can work, and any hard limits).
3. Selected applicants get a **15-minute call**, then a **paid 1-hour working trial** on the bar. It's a chance for you to see if you like us, too.

We reply to every applicant within **5 business days**. Target start date: **[date]**.

*[Café Name] is an equal opportunity employer. We hire people of all backgrounds, and we welcome applicants of every race, gender, age, ability, faith, and orientation. If you need an accommodation during the application process, email [email] and we'll make it work. We consider applicants with criminal records in line with [local fair-chance law].*

---

## Extras to go with the post

**Short version for Instagram, Indeed headline, or a window flyer:**
> **We're hiring a part-time barista!** 12-25 hrs/week, $[X]-$[Y]/hr + tips, paid training, free coffee, a schedule that respects your life. No experience needed, just warmth and curiosity. Apply: [link]

**Screening questions for the application form:**
1. Which days and hours are you available each week?
2. Can you work at least one weekend morning per week?
3. Describe a busy or stressful moment at work or school and how you handled it.
4. What's the best cup of coffee (or anything) you've ever had, and what made it good?
5. When could you start?

**What to fill in before posting:**
- Pay range and tip figure. Pay transparency is legally required in many places, and posts with a range get noticeably more applicants.
- Exact shift windows and whether you can guarantee minimum hours.
- Local law specifics: sick leave, fair-chance hiring, minimum age.
- One true detail that makes your café distinctive, such as your roaster, your neighborhood, or a signature drink. It will do more to attract the right people than any other line here.

I can tailor this to a specific café (name, location, vibe, pay) or draft a trainer checklist and interview scorecard to go with it.

**Hours:** [X–Y] hours per week
**Shifts:** Weekday mornings ([shift times]) and one weekend day ([Saturday or Sunday], [shift times])
**Tips:** [Describe policy, e.g., "Tips are pooled and split by hours worked, paid out weekly."]

## What you'll do

- Make espresso drinks and other beverages, consistently and to recipe
- Run the register and take orders accurately
- Keep the bar, counter, and equipment clean and stocked throughout your shift
- Greet customers warmly, and learn the regulars' names and orders
- Help with opening or closing tasks, depending on your shift

## What we're looking for

- Calm in a rush. Mornings get busy, and we need someone who stays steady
- Friendly and easy to talk to
- Reliable. You show up on time, and you tell us early if something changes
- Willing to learn. Experience is welcome but not required; we'll train you

## What you get
